stories.title: Waterfall Originates Loan for Disneyland Lodging Property
stories.excerpt: Waterfall Asset Management, on behalf of its clients, originated a $48-million senior mortgage loan to Dynamic City Capital (DCC) to fund the refinancing of the Portofino Inn & Suites Anaheim near Disneyland. DCC will use proceeds to fund capital improvements and to pay off its existing loan. Built in 2000 and renovated in 2012, the Portofino Inn & Suites Anaheim is a 190-key upper midscale hotel. The hotel’s amenities include an outdoor pool and a fitness center. Waterfall’s Commercial Real Estate team, led by Zachary Liebmann, worked closely with DCC to structure and execute the financing. JLL’s Hotels & Hospitality and Capital Markets Group served as the broker. “Waterfall’s investment in Portofino Inn & Suites Anaheim provides our firm an exciting opportunity to access a Disneyland market that continues to see strong demand,” said Doug Kosann, VP at Waterfall. “DCC’s well-established presence in this market made them an ideal partner, and we are pleased to help them both refinance their debt and fund renovations.” The post Waterfall Originates Loan for Disneyland Lodging Property appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.title: Northmarq Arranges Life Company Loan for Danbury Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s New York City Debt + Equity team, led by Ernest DesRochers and Kevin Toland, arranged a $10.5-million refinancing for Nutmeg Square Shopping Center, a 91,826-square-foot, grocery-anchored retail property located at 72 Newtown Rd. in Danbury, CT. The team arranged financing on behalf of the borrower through a correspondent life insurance company. The internal refinancing is structured as a construction-perm loan with a 10-year term. “This transaction highlights the strength of well-located grocery-anchored shopping centers and the importance of borrower-lender relationships in the evolving CRE lending markets,” DesRochers said. Situated on approximately 9.7 acres, Nutmeg Square is a neighborhood retail center with prominent frontage and signage along Newtown Road. The property is anchored by a new ShopRite supermarket, complementing a tenant roster that includes European Wax Center, Sally Beauty, Jersey Mike’s Subs, Supercuts, MyEyeDr., Little Caesars, Leslie’s Pool Supplies and several local service providers. stories.title: Alfred Equities Buying Starwood’s Former HQ in South Beach for $56M
stories.excerpt: Alfred Equities and entities tied to the May family are under contract to buy the former headquarters of Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Capital Group in Miami’s South Beach. The New York-based firm, led by Abraham B. Schwartz, plans to pay $55.8 million for the eight-story building at 1601 Washington Avenue, near the corner of 16th Street, near Lincoln Road and Collins Avenue. The 131,220-square-foot asset sits on a 1.4-acre site owned by the City Of Miami Beach. On Nov. 18, the city’s commission will consider waiving its right of first refusal to allow Alfred Equities’ acquisition of the ground lease to close. Under the agreement, Alfred Equities would own the asset alongside family trusts tied to Aryeh and Rivka May, as well as several limited partners, according to filings to Miami Beach. Built in 2002, the building features 106,652 square feet of office space, 28,483 square feet of retail space on the ground floor, and a 493-spot parking garage. The building, called The Lincoln, served as Starwood Capital Group’s headquarters from 2016 and 2022, before the investor moved up the road into a building it developed. The Lincoln became embroiled in controversy. In 2016, Elie Schwartz’s Nightingale Properties purchased the ground lease for $80 million through a crowdfunding platform. Nearly a decade later, Schwartz was sentenced to seven years in federal prison for defrauding investors by misappropriating millions in funds. In 2023, Robert Rivani’s Black Lion went under contract to buy the site for $82 million, The Real Deal reported, though the deal never closed. Two years later, the property fell under the control of lender Granite Point Mortgage Trust after it released a $84.7 million loan through a deed in lieu of foreclosure transaction. Alfred Equities’ pending purchase follows a string of office sales in Miami Beach, as wealthy executives seek offices near their homes. stories.title: Diamond Properties Acquires Industrial Park in Indianapolis from i3 Investors
stories.excerpt: JLL completed the sale of Shadeland Industrial Park, a 198,000-square-foot industrial portfolio located at 3221 N. Shadeland Ave., 3223-3229 N. Shadeland Ave. and 3241-3243 N. Shadeland Ave. in Indianapolis, Indiana. JLL represented the seller, i3 Investors, in the transaction. Diamond Properties acquired the asset. The JLL Capital Markets team was led by Senior Managing Director Sean Devaney and Senior Director Ross Bratcher, along with JLL leasing partners Executive Managing Director Brian Seitz and Senior Managing Director Brian Buschuk. Built in 1979, Shadeland Industrial Park consists of three Class B shallow-bay industrial buildings averaging 66,000 square feet each. The property is fully leased to two tenants across four suites, with occupancy serving the interior design and grocery retail sectors. The portfolio features clear heights ranging from 18 to 22 feet, 27 dock-high doors, 15 drive-in doors, wet sprinkler systems throughout, shared truck courts and is strategically positioned just east of downtown Indianapolis. stories.title: Peabody Companies Adds Senior Director of Operations
stories.excerpt: The Peabody Companies, a group of award-winning property management and real estate firms, has hired David McGuill of Sturbridge, MA as senior director of operations. He will work with Peabody’s site teams to understand their needs and develop practical strategies that support team members, communities and owners. McGuill brings 30 years of experience in affordable and market-rate multifamily property management to this position. Throughout his career, McGuill has led large portfolios and companywide initiatives focused on strengthening operations, improving efficiencies, and supporting high-performing teams, according to Peabody. “David has demonstrated that he’s an invested leader with a track record of strong performance in operational leadership, customer service, compliance, strategy development, and process improvement,” said Melissa Fish-Crane, principal and CEO of The Peabody Companies. “This, combined with his belief that strong operations begin with the people working within our communities every day, will make him an excellent fit for the Peabody team.” The post Peabody Companies Adds Senior Director of Operations appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.title: Oregon Neighborhood Center Acquired for $25.5M by Texas Investor
stories.excerpt: A Dallas, Texas-based real estate entity acquired Gresham Square, an 85,881-square-foot neighborhood shopping center in Gresham, Oregon, within the Portland metropolitan area. The property traded for $25.5 million, or $297 per square foot. Originally developed in 1973, the center sits on 8.72 acres at 56-360 Northwest Burnside Road. It is anchored by Wunderland, a longtime Oregon family entertainment operator, and features a diverse tenant roster that includes Raising Cane’s, Red Lobster, Dutch Bros. Coffee, Kaiser Permanente Dental Office, Providence Rehabilitation Services, Vancouver Clinic with Humana, Edward Jones and Plato’s Closet. Gresham Square was sold by Cumberland Holdings LLC, which acquired the property in 2014. The company made significant improvements to the center, including upgrading the façade and landscaping, expanding the Wunderland tenant from 8,000 to 38,000 square feet, and demolishing a 40,000-square-foot furniture store to create a 1.5-acre subdivided parcel leased to Raising Cane’s. Hanley Investment Group‘s Kevin Fryman, in association with ParaSell, Inc., represented Cumberland Holdings in the transaction. The buyer represented themselves. stories.title: Podcast: Fifth Dimension’s Kate Jarvis on How CRE Asset Managers Can Trust AI Agents
stories.excerpt: Kate Jarvis is the CEO and co-founder of Fifth Dimension, an agentic AI platform built for commercial real estate investment managers, asset managers and brokers. Fifth Dimension structures data from ERPs, CRMs, spreadsheets, PDFs and email into a unified system of record, then deploys prebuilt agents against the most commonly automated workflows in the industry. Prior to founding Fifth Dimension, Jarvis spent roughly a decade working at the intersection of financial services and commercial real estate technology. The company raised $26 million in 2026 and counts Boston Property Group, Realty Income and Peachtree Group among its clients. Kate is based in London. Recorded live from the floor at CREtech NY. stories.title: Forman Capital Lends $51M on North Carolina Shopping Center Project
stories.excerpt: Sagemark Development has landed $50.7 million of construction financing to build a shopping center in North Carolina’s Raleigh-Durham region, Commercial Observer has learned. Forman Capital supplied the loan for the developer’s Adams Crossing project in Sanford, N.C. The 223,153-square-foot development will be anchored by BJ’s Wholesale Club, Academy Sports + Outdoors and Burlington Stores. “Sanford is one of the fastest-growing communities in the Raleigh-Durham region, and the retail market is racing to keep up with the rooftops,” Scott Mehlman, Forman Capital partner and chief investment officer, said in a statement. “With BJ’s, Academy and Burlington anchoring the center, along with a strong mix of national retail, service and restaurant tenants, the project is positioned to perform from the day it opens.” Mehlman added that an existing Walmart next door to Adams Crossing is expected to drive additional foot traffic to the property. He originated the loan with a team that also included Ty Regnier, Mike Rediker and Ben Jacobson in a deal that closed Nov. 13. Located on a 32-acre site at 3350 NC-87 47 miles southwest of Downtown Ralegh, the Adams Crossings project is under construction and slated for completion in late 2027. Other tenants at the 95 percent pre-leased property will include Ulta Beauty, Five Below and Aspen Dental with Olive Garden and Longhorn Steakhouse occupying ground-leased outparcels. “Retail with this caliber of tenants and pre-leasing momentum is exactly where we want to be as a lender,” Jacobson, also a partner at Forman Capital, said in a statement. “Sagemark put together a project that will serve Sanford well for years to come.” Adams Crossing is in a growing area, with Lee County’s population growing 13 percent since 2020 to more than 70,000. The City of Sanford has also approved over 12,000 new residential units over the past five years, according to Forman. Sagemark Development did not immediately return a request for comment. stories.title: Former NBA Player Carlos Boozer of Impeccable: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Basketball fans remember Carlos Boozer as a two-time NBA All-Star who played power forward during a 13-year career that included seasons with the Cleveland Cavaliers, Utah Jazz, Chicago Bulls and Los Angeles Lakers. These days, the retired player is looking for shots and fighting for permission in the commercial real estate space. Boozer is co-founder and chief growth officer of Impeccable, a Boca Raton, Fla.-based company that has 50 restaurant locations open or under development. Impeccable is a franchisee operating locations of Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen, Del Taco and Freddy’s Frozen Custard & Steakburgers. “We’re going to be opening up offices in the Carolinas as well, but right now we have 7,500 square feet of office space in Boca, and we just signed a lease to expand that to 14,000 square feet,” Boozer said. “We are hiring rapidly as we’re growing.” Impeccable also is posting up for an expansion into multifamily development, Boozer said. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: You have a bit of a complicated business model – you’re finding and developing sites and also operating restaurants. Carlos Boozer: We own and operate Popeyes, Del Taco and Freddy’s. We typically buy the land, we’re landlords for some, and then we also own the operations of the restaurants. We are developing the Carolinas and branching out to some other states in the future, but we have a ton of restaurants, and we have some big centers that we’re building. We’re vertically integrated, so we have a great team that does site selection by the land. We lock it up, we develop, we do construction. We do everything in-house. We have a realty company, a development company, a construction company, and a marketing company. stories.title: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust, AWS Form $5B Data Center Joint Venture
stories.excerpt: Blackstone’s data center arm just came to a $5 billion agreement with Amazon Web Services (AWS). Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) — a publicly traded real estate investment trust that acquires and manages data centers — announced Monday that it has agreed to acquire a 75 percent interest in a joint-venture transaction with AWS for two data center campuses. The deals are valued at $5 billion and carry an initial cap rate of 7 percent for 13 powered-shell data centers across two AWS campuses, according to a release. AWS will lease the assets back from Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust on a triple-net basis — meaning Amazon will be responsible for rent, property taxes, property insurance, and common area maintenance — for at least 12 years, with extensions bringing the lease term for as long as 32 years. The assets are split between the greater Chicago region and Mississippi. “The quality, basis and tenant profile of these assets make this an attractive match for the deployment of our IPO proceeds,” said Nick Pell, CEO and president of Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust. “We believe BXDC is well positioned to capitalize on a highly compelling opportunity and deliver value for our shareholders.” Morgan Stanley, CBRE Capital Markets, Citi, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Wells Fargo served as financial advisers on the deal, which is expected to close before the end of the year. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
